themes.label: Building Commemoration
themes.rationale: The inscription records the reconstruction and repair of city fortifications, specifically seven towers and the surrounding walls, from their foundations.
themes.quote: τοὺς ἑπτὰ πύργους καὶ τὰ περὶ αὐτὰ τείχη ἀπὸ τοῦ θεμελίου ἀνέστησαν

themes.label: Honorific Inscriptions
themes.rationale: The text is dedicated to Emperor Marcus Aurelius and his sons, using his full imperial titles including Armeniacus, Parthicus, Medicus, and Germanicus.
themes.quote: Αὐτοκράτορι Καίσαρι Μ(άρκῳ) Αὐρηλίῳ Ἀντωνείνῳ [Ἀρμενιακῷ Παρθικῷ Μη]δικῷ Γ(ερμανικῷ) Αὐγούστῳ καὶ τοῖς υἱοῖς αὐτοῦ

themes.label: Prayers and Invocations
themes.rationale: The inscription begins with a formulaic religious invocation to Good Fortune and all the gods.

themes.label: Votive Dedications
themes.rationale: The construction work is presented as a dedication to the gods and the imperial family as a pious act of civic duty.

themes.label: Fragmentary
themes.rationale: The inscription is preserved in a fragmentary state with several lacunae that have been restored by epigraphists.

rationale: This inscription, dating to approximately 172-175 AD, commemorates the reconstruction of the defensive infrastructure of Kallatis. It specifically details the restoration of seven towers and the surrounding walls from their foundations. The project was executed during the governorship of Valerius Bradua and was spearheaded by local elites Titus Aelius Minicius Athanaion and his son Titus Aelius Minicius Moschion, both of whom held the high office of Pontarch of the Hexapolis.
